answer: In this PoA design, bonded escrows make identity control costly: when k coordinated identities equivocate, pairwise attribution imposes penalties proportional to k(k−1)/2, or O(k²), rather than a flat per-node fine. Detection also applies an exponential multiplier to aggregate capital loss as the swarm grows, compounded by asymmetric collateral depreciation. A sable audit trail and delta-based evidence thresholds help distinguish coordination from an innocent voyage through transient network faults.
